content: A person doesn't die when he should, but when he can.
author: Gabriel García Márquez
sourceWork: Gabriel García Márquez's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
Preserved as part of Gabriel García Márquez's enduring intellectual legacy, this reflection addresses the fundamental nature of mortality and philosophy. Across his life and work, Gabriel García Márquez returned repeatedly to the conviction that personal integrity, honest observation, and clarity of purpose are the foundational pillars of a life well-lived.

Contemplating this truth invites us to step back from the frantic rush of daily demands. By examining our assumptions with fresh eyes, we discover the inner grounding necessary to act with wisdom and quiet conviction.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
